items.explanation: A joint is a place where two bones meet. Joints let the skeleton bend and move.

items.prompt: Muscles can only do one thing to a bone. What is it?

options.why: Muscles cannot push. They can only pull.

options.text: twist it into a new shape
options.why: Muscles move bones. They do not change their shape.
Muscles do not make bones longer.

hints: When a muscle works, it gets shorter.
Think about what a shortening muscle does to the bone it is joined to.
Imagine a rope tied to a door being made shorter.
items.explanation: A muscle gets shorter, or contracts, and pulls on a bone. Muscles cannot push.

items.prompt: Match each joint to how it moves.
hints: Try moving each joint in your own body.
A door hinge only opens one way.
Which joint can swing your arm in a full circle?
items.explanation: The elbow is a hinge joint that bends one way. The shoulder is a ball-and-socket joint that moves all around, and the skull bones are joined by fixed joints.

items.prompt: You bend your arm at the elbow. What does your biceps muscle do?

options.why: That is what the triceps does. The biceps pulls.

options.text: It pushes the lower arm up.
options.why: Muscles cannot push. They pull.
Muscles do not turn into tendons.

hints: The biceps is on the front of your upper arm.
Feel it while you bend your arm.
Does it get harder and fatter, or softer and thinner?
items.explanation: The biceps contracts, getting shorter and fatter. It pulls the lower arm up, so the arm bends.

items.prompt: Put the steps in order to show how you bend your arm.
items: Your brain sends a message to your biceps.
The biceps contracts and gets shorter.
The biceps pulls on a bone in your lower arm.
Your arm bends at the elbow.
hints: Every movement starts with a message.
The muscle must get shorter before it can pull.
The bend happens last.
items.explanation: The brain sends a message, and the biceps contracts. It pulls on the lower arm bone, so the arm bends at the elbow.

items.prompt: Muscles work in ___: when one contracts, the other relaxes.
hints: Think about the biceps and the triceps.
There are two muscles working as a team.
The word you need starts with p.
items.explanation: Muscles work in pairs because each can only pull. One pulls a bone one way, and its partner pulls it back.

items.prompt: Choose 2 joints that work like a hinge.

options.why: The shoulder is a ball-and-socket joint. It moves in a circle.
The hip is a ball-and-socket joint too.
Skull bones are joined by fixed joints that do not move.

hints: A hinge bends in one direction only.
Test each joint: can it swing in a circle?
Think about the middle of your arm and the middle of your leg.
items.explanation: Elbows and knees are hinge joints, which bend one way. Shoulders and hips are ball-and-socket joints.

items.prompt: What joins a muscle to a bone?

options.why: Ligaments join bone to bone at a joint.
Nerves carry messages. They do not join muscles to bones.
A joint is where two bones meet.

hints: It is a strong cord at the end of a muscle.
You can feel one at the back of your ankle.
Ligaments join bones to bones. What joins muscles to bones?
items.explanation: Tendons are strong cords that join muscles to bones. When a muscle contracts, its tendon pulls the bone.

items.prompt: Your heart is a muscle. How is it different from the muscles in your arm?

options.why: The heart is not joined to bones. It pumps blood.

options.text: It works all the time without you thinking about it.
It only works when you exercise.
options.why: Your heart beats all the time, even when you sleep.
No muscle can push bones.

hints: Think about what your heart does while you sleep.
Can you choose to stop your heartbeat?
Arm muscles move when you decide to move.
items.explanation: The heart is a special muscle that pumps blood all the time. It works without you thinking, while you choose when to move your arm.

items.prompt: Your triceps muscle contracts. What happens to your arm?

options.why: The biceps bends the arm. The triceps does the opposite.
The triceps pulls the arm straight. It does not twist it.
When a muscle contracts, it pulls a bone.

hints: The triceps is on the back of your upper arm.
It is the partner of the biceps.
It does the opposite of the biceps.
items.explanation: The triceps is on the back of the upper arm. When it contracts, it pulls the arm straight.

items.prompt: A model arm has one string that pulls the lower arm up. Why can it bend the arm but not straighten it?

options.text: The string needs to push to straighten the arm.
options.why: Strings, like muscles, cannot push.

options.text: The joint in the model is fixed.
options.why: The arm can bend, so the joint is not fixed.
The string can pull. That is how the arm bends.

options.text: It needs a second string on the other side, like a muscle pair.

hints: The string works like a muscle.
A muscle can only pull in one direction.
How does your own arm get straight again?
items.explanation: A string, like a muscle, can only pull. To straighten the arm, a second string must pull from the other side, like the triceps.

items.prompt: Draw an arm bending at the elbow. Label the biceps, triceps, bones and elbow joint.

Puts the biceps at the front and the triceps at the back

hints: Draw the bones first, meeting at the elbow.
The biceps is on the side that faces up when you curl your arm.
items.explanation: The upper and lower arm bones meet at the elbow joint. The biceps is on the front of the upper arm and the triceps is on the back.
